text:
I found two things the spec doesn't say: no single finding for all unopened files, and SRC-AC7 pins the opposite, one finding per row.

`ARTIFACT gap_finding: Owner `plugins/temperspec-tgraph/docs/specs/session-record-checks.spec.md`: SRC-B5 (lines 46-48) says the expand check fails "naming the row and the path" when an existing file a row names has no opening in the session record. It states no single finding for all unopened files. SRC-B9 (81-83) limits what a finding may name to the rule file, row, path and phase, and says nothing of how many findings there are. SRC-AC7 (96) pins that the check names both of two rows that name one unread file, and says nothing of one finding. Per the triage note, `expand.spec.md` line 17 (`ts-exp-opened`) and a search of `docs/specs/` for "one finding" found nothing. Code: `plugins/temperspec-tgraph/workflow/temperspec/checks.py` `_opened_rows` (203-224; docstring 204-205 cites SRC-B5) makes one `_find("fail", ...)` per unopened row inside the loop (220-223). It names the row id and the path in each finding, and returns `found or [_ok(criterion)]`. So the read of the code is one finding per unopened row, not one for all. The test helper at `plugins/temperspec-tgraph/tests/test_session_record_checks.py:197` filters findings by `ts-exp-opened`. A rewrite of SRC-B5 and SRC-AC7 is needed so one finding names every unopened path, and with it the code and the tests that count findings. Rows that share a path must still all be named, per SRC-AC7. Path and rows stay allowed by SRC-B9.`
